pisharp - AI coding assistant with read, bash, edit, write tools

Usage:
  pisharp [options] [--] [@files...] [messages...]

Commands:
  pisharp install <source> [-l]     Install extension source and add to settings
  pisharp remove <source> [-l]      Remove extension source from settings
  pisharp uninstall <source> [-l]   Alias for remove
  pisharp update [source|self|pi]   Update pi, extensions, or model catalogs
  pisharp list                      List installed extensions from settings
  pisharp config [-l]               Open TUI to enable/disable package resources (Tab switches scope)
  pisharp auth <command>            Print credentials or check provider readiness
  pisharp mcp <command>             Check MCP servers, sign in to or out of OAuth servers
  pisharp session <verb>            PiSharp explicit-path session commands (create, prompt, resume, rpc, terminal, ...)
  pisharp durable [options]         EXPERIMENTAL: PiSharp's crash-safe durable agent (--continue, --tier <tier>)
  pisharp <command> --help          Show help for install/remove/uninstall/update/list/config/auth/mcp/session/durable

Options:
  --provider <name>              Provider to search for --model (requires --model)
  --model <pattern>              Model pattern or ID (supports "provider/id" and optional ":<thinking>")
  --api-key <key>                API key (defaults to env vars)
  --system-prompt <text>         System prompt (default: coding assistant prompt)
  --append-system-prompt <text>  Append text or file contents to the system prompt (can be used multiple times)
  --mode <mode>                  Output mode: text (default), json, or rpc
  --print, -p                    Non-interactive mode: process prompt and exit
  --continue, -c                 Continue previous session
  --resume, -r                   Select a session to resume
  --session <path|id>            Use specific session file or partial UUID
  --session-id <id>              Use exact project session ID, creating it if missing
  --fork <path|id>               For

  pisharp install ssh://git@github.com/user/repo

Usage:
  pisharp update [source|self|pi] [--self|--extensions|--models|--all] [--extension <source>] [--approve|--no-approve] [--force]

Update pi, installed packages, or model catalogs.

Options:
  --self                  Update pi only (default when no target is given)
  --extensions            Update installed packages only
  --models                Refresh model catalogs only
  --all                   Update pi and installed packages
  --extension <source>    Update one package only
  -a, --approve           Trust project-local files for this command
  -na, --no-approve       Ignore project-local files for this command
  --force                 Reinstall pi even if the current version is latest

Short forms:
  pisharp update                Update pi only
  pisharp update --all          Update pi and all extensions
  pisharp update --models       Refresh model catalogs only
  pisharp update <source>       Update one package
  pisharp update pi             Update pi only (self works as alias to pi)

Usage:
  pisharp mcp add <server> [options] -- <command> [args...]
  pisharp mcp add <server> [options] --url <url>
  pisharp mcp remove <server> [-l]
  pisharp mcp list [--json]
  pisharp mcp login <server> [--timeout <seconds>]
  pisharp mcp logout <server>

Configure and check MCP servers and sign in to OAuth servers without starting a session.
Reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json and, in trusted projects, .pi/mcp.json.

Commands:
  add <server>            Add or replace a server in mcp.json
  remove <server>         Remove a server from mcp.json
  list                    Show state, tools, and errors (exits 1 on failure)
  login <server>          Sign in through the browser
  logout <server>         Delete the stored OAuth credentials

Options for add and remove:
  -l, --local             Use .pi/mcp.json in the current project instead of the global file

Options for add:
  --url <url>             Streamable HTTP server URL (instead of a command)
  --env <KEY=VALUE>       Environment variable for a stdio server (repeatable)
  --cwd <dir>             Working directory for a stdio server
  --header <KEY=VALUE>    HTTP header (repeatable)
  --bearer-token-env-var <NAME>
                          Send "Authorization: Bearer ${NAME}"
  --oauth-client-id <id>  Pre-registered OAuth client id
  --oauth-client-secret <secret>
                          OAuth client secret (may be ${NAME} or !command)
  --oauth-callback-port <port>
                          Fixed OAuth callback port
  --oauth-client-name <name>
                          Client name sent when registering with the OAuth server
  --exposure <mode>       codemode (default), deferred, direct, or hidden
  --description <text>    What the server offers, shown in the system prompt

Other options:
  --json                  Print the list as JSON
  --timeout <seconds>     Time limit for the whole sign-in (default: 300)

Usage:
  pisharp session <verb> [options]
  pisharp session <verb> --help

PiSharp's explicit-path session commands, for tests and scripted runs. Paths are absolute, tools use the explicit
tool policy and reach only what the --allow-* options grant, and most verbs run against an offline script of
provider responses (--offline-script). A bad command line prints one JSON line and exits with code 2.

Verbs:
  create                       Create a session file in a workspace
  prompt, resume               Send one --message and save the answer
  inspect, tree, history       Print a session's entries, tree or message history
  rpc                          Speak the RPC protocol over stdin and stdout (--offline-script or --live)
  chat                         Read prompts and slash commands from stdin
  terminal                     Open the terminal UI (--terminal-preview or --live)
  list                         List the sessions in --session-store folders
  copy-inspect, copy, migrate  Check, copy or migrate a session file
  context-edit                 Replace the content of one entry
  compact, branch-summary      Compact a session or summarize a branch
